exposure: Half-day outpatient management of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM)
outcome: Blood glucose levels (fasting, 1 hour post-sugar intake, 2 hours post-sugar intake, before meals, 2 hours after meals, at bedtime before delivery)
Maternal complications (hypertensive diseases during pregnancy, postpartum hemorrhage)
Infant complications (low-weight infants, neonatal asphyxia, stillbirth, polyamniotic fluid, premature rupture of membranes, macrosomia, neonatal hypoglycemia, neonatal hyperbilirubinemia)
cohort: 4674 pregnant women diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus in the Woman and Child Care Center of Qinhuangdao City between January 2020 and December 2022.
finding: Half-day outpatient management of GDM effectively controlled maternal blood glucose levels and significantly reduced complications such as macrosomia, neonatal hypoglycemia, and neonatal hyperbilirubinemia, without significant differences in other measured adverse maternal or infant outcomes.
followup_time: Observations were taken up to the immediate postnatal period, covering perinatal complications.
birth_weight: Complications related to birth weight, specifically macrosomia and low-weight infants, were observed.
